themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints surged to 6 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 4700% spike (z-score: 17.76)—suggesting rapid deterioration of vacant or abandoned properties across Bed-Stuy that may indicate illegal dumping, neglect, or property abandonment tied to the active ULURP rezonings.
evidence: 6 lot condition complaints filed this week vs. 0.1 per-week 8-week average (4700% increase, z-score: 17.76)
Signal emerged this week with no prior sustained pattern, indicating rapid onset
Coincides with multiple active ULURP rezonings (1166 Bedford, 862-868 Kent, Constellation CB3) that may displace or destabilize property maintenance
reporting_angles: Canvass neighborhoods with highest complaint density to photograph and identify which lots are at issue; interview residents about what changed this week
Cross-reference lot complaints with ULURP timeline and DOB permits (883 filings in 90 days) to test whether development speculation is triggering property abandonment

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints jumped to 9 this week compared to a 1.4 per-week baseline—a 554% spike (z-score: 4.84)—marking an acute escalation in branch removal, cutting, or environmental vandalism this week, especially concerning given community board's repeated requests for park and green space investment.
evidence: 9 illegal tree damage complaints filed this week vs. 1.4 per-week 8-week average (554% increase, z-score: 4.84)
Spike is THIS WEEK only; no prior sustained elevation
Community board has filed recurring budget requests for new/expanded parks and green space amenities (01 request), suggesting tree canopy is valued community asset
reporting_angles: Visit specific streets cited in complaints to document damaged trees and interview eyewitnesses about who cut them and why
Interview NYC Parks enforcement about whether there is active tree-poaching activity or illegal contractor work tied to construction permits (162 new building permits filed in 90 days)

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints spiked to 19 this week versus a 3.1 per-week baseline—a 508% increase (z-score: 10.34)—indicating a sharp uptick in low-level quality-of-life or safety concerns this week that may signal deteriorating public order or heightened resident anxiety.
evidence: 19 non-emergency police complaints filed this week vs. 3.1 per-week 8-week average (508% increase, z-score: 10.34)
Spike is acute and emerged this week with no prior escalation pattern
Converges with obstruction spike (12 complaints this week vs. 3.4 avg, +256%) suggesting street-level disorder or blocking of public space
reporting_angles: Request NYPD 73rd Precinct data on the nature of non-emergency calls this week (loitering, trespassing, street vending, etc.) to identify root cause
Interview residents in highest-complaint blocks about what prompted calls and whether they feel safe

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints (missing + damaged) totaled 6 this week versus 0.8 per-week baseline—a combined 650% spike across two sign-related categories—suggesting systematic maintenance failure or vandalism of directional and regulatory signage this week.
evidence: 3 street sign - missing complaints + 3 street sign - damaged complaints = 6 total this week (combined z-scores: 6.35 missing, 4.91 damaged)
Missing signs: 3 this week vs. 0.2 per-week baseline (1100% increase). Damaged signs: 3 this week vs. 0.6 per-week baseline (380% increase)
Both categories spiked THIS WEEK; no prior sustained pattern
reporting_angles: Photograph affected intersections to assess whether signs are missing/damaged in clusters (suggesting targeted vandalism) or scattered (suggesting maintenance gaps)
Contact NYC DOT to determine if budget cuts, staffing shortages, or known vandalism ring are responsible

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bike Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints peaked at 7 three weeks ago versus a 0.6 per-week baseline—a 1020% spike (z-score: 13.17)—indicating that bike-share or personal bike abandonment may be a lingering sidewalk obstruction and storage problem in the district.
evidence: 7 abandoned bike complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 per-week 8-week average (1020% increase, z-score: 13.17)
Spike occurred 3 weeks ago and does not appear to be ongoing THIS WEEK, making this lower priority than active spikes
Converges with obstruction spike (12 this week, +256%) suggesting sidewalk blocking remains a recurring issue
reporting_angles: Assess whether spike was tied to a specific bike-share event, redistribution, or weather event 3 weeks ago
Interview residents about whether abandoned bikes remain a persistent visual/accessibility problem even if new complaints have declined
